findings.message: This ADD copies only local files; COPY is the more predictable instruction for that.
This apt-get install has no -y (or --yes), so it will wait on a prompt no build can answer.
This apt-get install has no --no-install-recommends, so it pulls in every recommended package too.
This RUN does not remove /var/lib/apt/lists afterwards, so the package index stays in this layer.
This RUN upgrades every installed package, which depends on whatever versions are current on the mirror at build time.
This RUN uses cd to change directory; that only affects this one RUN. Use WORKDIR to change it for every instruction that follows.
This COPY --from="build" names no earlier stage in this file.
The stage name "base" is already used earlier in this file.
The EXPOSE port "70000" is not a number from 1 to 65535.
The EXPOSE protocol "bogus" is neither tcp nor udp.
The EXPOSE protocol "TCP" should be written lowercase.
The base image "node:latest" is pinned to the "latest" tag, which moves over time.
The base image "node" has no explicit tag, so it resolves to "latest" today and possibly something else tomorrow.
"RUN" appears before the first FROM instruction; the Dockerfile reference allows only ARG there.
This ENV uses the legacy "key value" form with no equals sign.
MAINTAINER is deprecated; use a LABEL to record an image author instead.
This CMD instruction's JSON array form is malformed and could not be parsed: Expected ',' or ']' after array element in JSON at position 20 (line 1 column 21).
This stage already has an earlier CMD; only the last one takes effect.
No USER instruction sets a non-root user in the final stage, so the image runs as root by default.
The name "API_TOKEN" looks like it holds a secret; ENV is visible in the build history or the running container.
This CMD uses shell form; the JSON array form avoids an intermediate shell that would not forward signals.
The stage name "Base" should be lowercase.
This RUN uses sudo, which has unpredictable behaviour inside a build and crosses no real privilege boundary here.

This FROM instruction uses "VERSION", which was not declared with ARG and a default value before the first FROM instruction, so it would resolve to an empty, invalid image reference unless the build supplies one.
"FOOBAR" is not an instruction the Dockerfile reference defines.
This here-document has no line containing only its terminator "EOF".
This WORKDIR "app" is relative, and no earlier WORKDIR in this stage set an absolute starting point.
